insert_after: With only this one source, the two rate changes have correlation $-1$: one rises whenever the other falls. Adding independent private noise lowers the magnitude. The negative covariance here comes from opposite tuning slopes under a common position change. It does not establish an inhibitory connection between the cells.
intro: For the same slopes, set both expected rates to 10 Hz at the starting position. The upper plot shows the fixed rate curves; the lower plot shows their changes under a common position displacement.
caption: A common displacement of $+0.1$ m increases rate 1 by $0.2$ Hz and decreases rate 2 by $0.1$ Hz. The changes lie on one line. With displacement variance $0.01$ m², their covariance is $-0.02$ Hz² and their correlation is $-1$. The 10 Hz baseline is chosen only to display positive rates. These are exact lines from the guide’s local example, not recorded data.
alt: The upper plot shows two fixed linear tuning curves with slopes plus two and minus one hertz per meter, crossing at ten hertz. Moving from zero to plus 0.1 meter raises the first rate by 0.2 hertz and lowers the second by 0.1 hertz. The lower plot puts the paired rate changes on a downward sloping line through zero, with that example marked.
interpretation: Both changes are set by the same position displacement, so they occupy one direction in the two-rate plane. Independent private fluctuations would spread them away from that line.
source_locator: Guide reconstruction: Chapter6, How a static map can carry a moving estimate and Example: opposite rate changes from the same position error. The joint construction is not reported as a tested model in any of the three papers.
